newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa Q1 current account deficit 1.9 bln rand.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa Q1 current account deficit 1.9 bln rand.

text.p: South Africa recorded a deficit of 1.869 billion rand on the current account of the balance of payments in the three months to March 31, 1997, the Reserve Bank said on Thursday.

Economists polled by Reuters had forecast a consensus deficit of 2.1 billion rand, with the range 0.5 to 3.0 billion, after a negligible 50 million rand current account gap in the last quarter of 1996.
The Reserve Bank said in its latest Quarterly Bulletin that the widening of the deficit was largely because of an unexpected decline in the quantity of relatively price-insensitive goods exported.
The decline in total exports was exacerbated by a fall in the dollar and the rand price of gold.

On a seasonally-adjusted and annualised basis, the deficit increased to 7.9 billion rand from 4.7 billion in the fourth quarter of 1996. As a ratio of GDP, the deficit stood at 1.4 percent in the first quarter against an average of 1.6 percent in 1996.
